profile.lead: Green Lantern is a name several heroes have carried, not a single person.
profile.summary:
The first was Alan Scott. Martin Nodell created him, with Bill Finger on the early stories, and he debuted in All-American Comics #16 in 1940. After a train crash, Scott came into a magic lantern and crafted a ring from it. He had to recharge that ring against the lantern, and he used it on ordinary criminals before joining the Justice Society of America. His power was magic. The Lanterns who followed are something else.

The Green Lantern most readers know arrived in 1959. Writer John Broome and artist Gil Kane introduced Hal Jordan, a test pilot, in Showcase #22. A dying alien, Abin Sur, passes him a power ring and the post of Green Lantern for Earth. The ring belongs to the Green Lantern Corps, an interstellar law-enforcement agency overseen by the Guardians of the Universe. Willpower is the fuel. The ring lets its wearer fly, and the green light it throws can become a force field or a solid object, limited mostly by imagination and nerve. The oath that comes with it still opens the way readers know it: in brightest day, in blackest night, no evil shall escape my sight.

Other officers have held the name since. Guy Gardner was next, remembered for a stubborn streak. John Stewart arrived in 1972, written by Dennis O'Neil and drawn by Neal Adams: an architect chosen as Hal's backup, and one of DC's first Black superheroes. He refused a mask. A later story gave him a past in the U.S. Marines. Kyle Rayner, an artist, took up a ring after the Corps was destroyed. Simon Baz, Jessica Cruz, and Sojourner Mullein followed, the last of them posted to the Far Sector. The light stays green. The job is a sector of space.

Lanterns puts two of those officers, Hal Jordan and John Stewart, on a murder case in the American heartland.

profile.summary: Batman is Bruce Wayne. Bob Kane and Bill Finger introduced him in Detective Comics #27 (1939). He has no powers. He prepares, and he does not leave a case alone. Clayface, an actor whose body turns to clay, is one of the foes those cases keep producing.
